name: Cloudera, Inc. (including Hortonworks)
subcategory: Hadoop / big-data platform; hybrid data cloud
origin_detail: Formed 2008-06-27 in Burlingame, California by Christophe Bisciglia, Amr Awadallah, Jeff Hammerbacher and Mike Olson; Hadoop co-creator Doug Cutting joined in 2009. Rival Hortonworks was spun out of Yahoo's Hadoop team in June 2011 with $23M from Yahoo and Benchmark, built its products on open-source Apache projects, and merged with Cloudera in January 2019. HQ Santa Clara, California.
openness_notes: Cloudera distributed Apache Software Foundation projects (Hadoop, Hive, Spark and others) with its own management software; Hortonworks built on open-source projects. After the merger, new releases became subscription-only from November 2019, and from 2021-01-31 all Cloudera software, including legacy CDH and HDP, requires a paid subscription to access. Coded open core (2). A 2019 pledge to release all components under open-source licences is recalled but was not confirmed in fetched pages; if it holds, the code would rate 3 with gated binaries.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 ASF components + Cloudera management software
license_history.note: Licensing of Cloudera's own management tools not confirmed in fetched pages.

license_history.license: All Cloudera software (incl. legacy CDH, HDP, HDF) requires a valid subscription from 2021-01-31
license_history.note: Expired subscriptions lose patches; clusters keep running.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Distribution was closed rather than the licence; the underlying projects stay at the ASF.

exit_events.note: Hortonworks went public in 2014 (Wikipedia category); terms not confirmed.
Cloudera IPO 2017-04-28; price and valuation not confirmed in fetched pages.
All-stock merger of equals announced October 2018 (CNBC), completed January 2019.
Announced about 2021-06-01 (WSJ); all-cash deal of about $5.3B completed October 2021. Per-share price not confirmed.

risk_events: 2019-06: CEO Tom Reilly and co-founder Mike Olson left after the merger
2019-2021: Binaries moved behind a subscription paywall
2026-10: Settlement with the US government over PERM (green card) irregularities, per Wikipedia citing Newsweek (unverified)
robustness: The Hadoop-ecosystem projects are ASF-governed, so the technology does not depend on Cloudera. The company is PE-owned since 2021 and buys AI tooling (Verta, June 2024).
openness_effect_assessment: Both an open-core firm (Cloudera) and a more fully open one (Hortonworks) reached public markets (2017 and 2014), but neither sustained independent growth: they merged in 2019, gated binaries behind subscriptions, and sold to private equity for about $5.3B in 2021, not far above the roughly $4.1B implied by Intel's 2014 investment. Openness built the ecosystem but did not secure either company's independence.
key_takeaway: Cloudera and Hortonworks are the Hadoop era's natural experiment in degrees of openness. Both IPO'd, neither thrived alone, they merged, the combined firm closed distribution rather than the licence, and private equity took it private in 2021. The Apache projects outlived both companies' independence.
